blocks.item: In the workspace where you added your collection, go to Collections.
Click the OneAPI collection folder name.

Go to the Variables tab displayed for the collection. The variables present in the collection are displayed in a table, with values prepopulated for variables that are universal to all organizations (e.g., base URL for APIs).

Ensure that the variables are selected and configured properly. For variables that contain values specific to the organization, such as client ID, client secret, Authentication Service's token endpoint, etc., you must configure the values manually. For each variable, enter its value into the Initial value column, then re-enter the same value in the Current value column.
The following table shows the variables and a description of their values:

table: API client ID obtained from Authentication Service.
API client secret obtained from Authentication Service.

Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) tenant ID of the customer obtained from Authentication Service or ZPA. To learn how to obtain the ZPA customer ID, see Getting Started. This configuration is applicable only to ZPA API clients.
This variable is prepopulated with the base URL for OneAPI: https://api.zsapi.net.

This variable is prepopulated with the base URL for Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) API: {{oneAPIBaseUrl}}/zia/api/v1, which would become https://api.zsapi.net/zia/api/v1 when the {{oneAPIBaseUrl}} variable is replaced with its value.
This variable is prepopulated with the base URL for ZPA API: {{oneAPIBaseUrl}}/zpa, which would become https://api.zsapi.net/zpa when the {{oneAPIBaseUrl}} variable is replaced with its value.

This variable is prepopulated with the base URL for Client Connector API: {{oneAPIBaseUrl}}/zcc/papi/public, which would become https://api.zsapi.net/zcc/papi/public when the {{oneAPIBaseUrl}} variable is replaced with its value.

Represents Authentication Service's token endpoint: https://<Vanity Domain>.zslogin.net, where <Vanity Domain> refers to the domain name used by your organization.
